angle: Tools don’t fix process—redesign the product development system or your AI copilot will stall.
sourceTitle: Beyond the copilot: Scaling the agentic product development life cycle
linkedinPost:
An AI copilot won’t fix a broken software lifecycle.

A recent McKinsey piece argues the teams seeing real gains are redesigning their entire product development system, not just rolling out tools. That matches what I see on the ground.

Where we’ve moved the needle, we didn’t “add AI to Jira.” We rebuilt workflows and decision rights around it. Example: we cut PR cycle time by 30% by letting agents auto-generate tests, propose fixes, and route edge cases to the right reviewer—paired with new guardrails and clear rollback paths.

We also shifted metrics. Instead of counting “AI suggestions,” we track lead time for changes, escaped defects, incidents per deploy, and cost-to-serve per feature. And we rewrote roles: TLs own evaluation harnesses, QA owns safety gates, and product owns the acceptance criteria the agents optimize for.

The pattern: pick two or three chokepoints (test data creation, regression triage, documentation drift), redesign the flow end-to-end with agents in the loop, and only then scale.

If your “gen AI program” is a tool rollout, you’ll get pilot wins that never add up. If it’s an operating-model change, you’ll see compounding impact.

Where would a full-flow redesign beat a tool drop in your org? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #ForwardDeployedEngineer
